mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 10% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 10% but S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increase, it indicates a strong labor market, boosting S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 25% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, if federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4%, it leads to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is above 4% but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased supply and economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production grows but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI (CPIAUCSL) level above 220 indicates high inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPI exceeds 220 but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) both increase, it signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 20% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, slowing payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) indicates potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If payroll growth slows but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time.
